title: Match the Activity to the Skill
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Classify ten afternoon activities by the human skill each one builds most directly: collaboration, communication, empathy, creativity, or computational thinking.

learningObjectives: The learner will classify ten afternoon activities by the human skill each builds most directly, correctly placing at least eight of ten on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Collaboration, communication skills, empathy, creativity, computational thinking, and the activity-skill matrix, from Chapters 12, 13, and 14

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit an answer, get feedback with the reason, and review what was missed
keyQuestions: What does this activity ask students to do most directly?
What second skill does it build?
commonMisconceptions: Each activity builds only one skill
Technical activities do not need collaboration
assessmentOpportunities: A robotics team designs, builds, and debugs a robot together. Primary skill?
Do arts activities build only creativity?

controls.name: Choice buttons
controls.description: commit an answer. A wrong first answer gives a hint and lets you choose again; only the first answer counts.

controls.name: Show definitions
controls.description: opens or closes the reference table. Reading it is exploration, not evidence.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves to the next item after feedback. On the results screen, Previous missed and Next missed step through what you missed.

controls.name: Play again
controls.description: starts a practice run with the items reshuffled. Practice runs do not change the first-run score.
